Australian subsidiary Sun Metals (Townsville) has 270 thousand tonnes a year of zinc capacity at 100% utilisation (H1 2026 zinc output 122,761 MT). Consolidated H1 2026 purchases of property, plant and equipment KRW 529,414,924,914.

quarterly_data.signal: US integrated non-ferrous smelter (new business section): Korea Zinc is building an integrated smelter in Tennessee through subsidiary Crucible Metals, LLC on the former Nyrstar smelter site, in partnership with the US government; construction to start in 2026, build 2027-2029, phased trial operation targeted for 2029, producing 13 non-ferrous metals including 11 critical minerals plus semiconductor-grade sulfuric acid - annually 300 thousand tonnes of zinc, 200 thousand tonnes of lead, 35,000 tonnes of copper and 5,100 tonnes of rare metals. Total expected investment about USD 7,432 million (about KRW 10.9 trillion). The business alliance with Crucible JV LLC covers critical minerals including antimony and gallium. On 04-01-2026 Korea Zinc acquired four Nyrstar US companies (Nyrstar Clarksville Inc, Nyrstar Tennessee Mines - Strawberry Plains LLC, Nyrstar Tennessee Mines - Gordonsville LLC, Nyrstar US Trading Inc), with a germanium royalty contract tied to future germanium output.
quarterly_data.figure: USD 7,432 million total investment; 300 kt zinc, 200 kt lead, 35,000 t copper, 5,100 t rare metals a year; trial operation 2029

quarterly_data.signal: Critical-minerals R&D (half-year report): the 2025 R&D record lists development of a high-purity gallium recovery process (to stabilise the strategic-mineral supply chain), a germanium recovery process from by-products, a tellurium recovery process from copper electrolyte and higher antimony recovery from zinc and lead residues; on 02-23-2026 the board approved a change to the germanium recovery facility investment.

Company market outlook (half-year report): for Q3 2026 precious metals the company expects range-bound trading, with central-bank gold buying, silver's structural supply shortage and growing medium-to-long-term industrial demand from AI data-center and power-infrastructure investment supporting prices; for copper it expects medium-to-long-term demand growth from expanding AI and data-center investment and continued upward price pressure.

Supplier Glencore: raw-material table of the half-year report names Glencore (and others) as supplier of the parent's zinc concentrate (H1 2026 purchases KRW 1,066,207M) and lead concentrate (KRW 4,120,133M); concentrate is secured under long-term contracts with several overseas companies.
